A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HAI-Eval and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–M. Complete text and visual comparisons support reliable judgments.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five LLMs and a 45-participant study, including performance, task validation, questionnaire results, and a collaboration case study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original LLM evaluations, participant study, validation results, questionnaire analyses, and case study in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The template bank, GPT-4.1 task-generation agent and its four tools, cloud IDE, HAI-EC evaluation pipeline, and scoring procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Python tasks across SDE, MLE, and DS tracks, three difficulty levels, 45 templates, and 450 static instances. Human-study population and task scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain Claude-Sonnet-4, Claude-Sonnet-3.7, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, and Gemini-2.5-Pro, with identical comparison membership in Tables 1, 6, and 7. Revised citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The four experimental conditions, 45-participant counterbalanced design, four tasks per participant, model settings, time limits, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Removing the MacKenzie (2002) citation does not alter the stated study protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same validation analyses in Appendices B and D, procedural-failure comparison, participant and order-effect analyses, and Clickomania case study in Appendix L. No ablation, robustness test, or case evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Standard-deviation reporting in Tables 3 and 9 and Figure 11, and inter-rater agreement reporting in Table 5, are unchanged. There are no changes to disclosed repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 2 retains average overall pass@1 rates of 18.89%, 0.67%, 2.89%, and 31.11% for CH, C0, C1, and C2, respectively.

T1.justification: The collaboration constraints in Equation 1 and template-acceptance conditions in Equation 2 are identical. Citation revisions around their motivation introduce no mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same unified-benchmark contribution, dual evaluation interfaces, higher-order reasoning claims, and human–AI co-reasoning claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reasoning limitations and collaborative synergy are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning Python-only coverage, Copilot-supported models, participant demographics, and discretized performance metrics.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, agent hyperparameters and prompts, validation instructions, intervention rules, study materials, and repository-maintenance disclosures are unchanged. No new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Fujikawa et al. (2024) and Rangarajan et al. (2024) references. Most other apparent substitutions match existing works through their titles or arXiv identifiers, including the surveys relabeled from Zhang to Jin and Xin to Dong. The substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an equal-contribution marker for Zhimu Huang and revises numerous citation labels and bibliography records. Explanatory prose, section order, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography edits change wrapping, typography, and entry placement across pages 12–18, with limited citation-related reflow elsewhere. All figures and tables retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a limited editorial improvement: it removes duplicated author names from the Kamsties reference and supplies publisher, edition, and ISBN details for MacKenzie (2024). These visible repairs improve reference clarity and completeness. The methods, empirical evidence, scientific arguments, and limitations remain unchanged.
